history.content: What different forms of information do I need from my cloned repositories in order to set up my application?

It appears that you will need access to the code and any associated submodules within your cloned repositories to set up your application. By default, the Git clone in the pipelines does not clone the submodules in a repository. However, you can enable cloning the submodules in the user repositories by setting the opt-in flag `opt-in-clone-submodules` to 1. The `.gitmodules` file in the Git repository must use either HTTPS URLs or relative URLs for the submodules to be cloned. Additionally, you may need to configure any necessary dependencies, build instructions, and deployment scripts, which are typically found in a README file or a similar documentation within the repository.

To configure cloning of Git submodules, you can follow these steps:
1. Enable cloning of the submodules by setting the opt-in flag `opt-in-clone-submodules` to  1 to enable cloning of the submodules
2. Set the opt-in flag opt-in-clone-submodules-with-remote to 1 to enable cloning of the submodules by using the status of the submodule’s remote-tracking branch to update the submodule, rather than the superproject’s recorded SHA-1.
